title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — November 27, 2026
summary: Adversaries are scaling AI-driven attacks against critical infrastructure and software supply chains, highlighted by confirmed AI-agent breaches of Swiss critical infrastructure (The Hacker News), DPRK's PolinRider poisoning 7,600+ GitHub repositories (The Hacker News), and a 12-year-old pre-auth remote root flaw in the Linux kernel NFS server (BleepingComputer).

tier1.title: 1. New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: BleepingComputer

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Linux Kernel / CVE-2026-99362 (CVSS 9.8 Pre-Auth RCE)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server (nfsd) allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute code as root. Crafted requests overflow a kernel buffer, leak memory to defeat KASLR, and run commands as root upon connection close. Export rules do not stop the exploit, making any reachable NFS server vulnerable across the Linux ecosystem.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Upgrade Linux kernels to 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61, or 7.3.2 immediately, or strictly block TCP port 2049 at the network perimeter.

tier1.title: 2. Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Critical Infrastructure / Autonomous AI Intrusion (Active Breach)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Switzerland's national cybersecurity agency confirmed that attackers utilizing autonomous AI agents successfully breached four out of five targeted Swiss organizations. Three of the targets were critical infrastructure operators, with two resulting in successful system compromises. This marks a watershed moment of state-confirmed, AI-agent-executed breaches against national critical infrastructure.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Review anomaly detection thresholds for high-velocity, automated lateral movement and ensure critical infrastructure control planes are segmented from IT networks.

tier1.title: 3. North Korea-Linked PolinRider Poisons Over 7,600 GitHub Repositories to Spread Malware

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain / DPRK Malware Campaign (Mass Compromise)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: The DPRK-linked PolinRider campaign has poisoned over 7,600 legitimate developer GitHub repositories since February 2025. Attackers plant a malicious Python loader inside 'utils' packages or conftest.py files that executes automatically upon import to deliver next-stage payloads. With 86% of compromised repos belonging to real developers rather than throwaway accounts, this represents a massive open-source supply chain hazard.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Audit Python dependencies and CI/CD pipelines for unauthorized modifications to conftest.py or utility packages, and pin third-party GitHub dependencies to verified commit hashes.

tier2.title: 1. Chinese and North Korean state hackers add ARTEX AI framework to their arsenal

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence & AI

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Microsoft Threat Intelligence warned that state-sponsored hacking groups tied to Beijing and Pyongyang have adopted the open-source ARTEX AI pentesting framework. Released on GitHub in July 2026, ARTEX uses LLM agents to autonomously plan and execute reconnaissance, credential attacks, and exploitation based on high-level operator goals.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Nation-state actors are rapidly operationalizing open-source LLM agent frameworks for autonomous offensive operations.; Defenders must prepare for machine-speed reconnaissance and exploitation chains that adapt dynamically to target environments.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: ARTEX is an LLM-driven open-source penetration testing framework that runs attacks largely on its own, with the operator setting a goal and AI agents planning and carrying it out.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security

tier2.title: 2. SAP Security Incident: Stolen GitHub Tokens and Source Code Risk

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Application & Enterprise Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: SAP confirmed it took urgent measures after attackers used stolen employee authentication tokens to access and alter source code on GitHub. While SAP states there is no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data, the compromise highlights persistent risks surrounding developer credential hygiene.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Stolen employee GitHub tokens enabled both source code exfiltration and unauthorized code alteration.; Organizations must enforce hardware-backed MFA, short-lived tokens, and strict branch protection rules on source code repositories.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Attackers had stolen authentication tokens belonging to SAP employees and used them to access and alter source code on GitHub.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SOCRadar

tier2.title: 3. 1Password was breached through an employee's GitHub account

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Identity & Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Attackers compromised a 1Password employee's GitHub account to push malicious code to backend services, reaching the CI/CD system and exfiltrating source code and customer metadata. Stolen data includes customer names, emails, account IDs, and SRP verifiers, though password vaults and Secret Keys remained uncompromised.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Customer vaults held firm due to end-to-end encryption and Secret Key architecture, preventing direct credential theft.; Exfiltrated customer emails and metadata create a high risk of targeted phishing and fake recovery email campaigns.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The attacker pushed malicious code to backend services, pulled source code and customer records, and reached the CI/CD system.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 4. Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Web Application Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The Drupal security team warned that attackers are actively exploiting a second critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-136716) allowing complete takeover of unpatched websites. The flaw affects roughly 31,500 internet-facing installations left in residual or incomplete install states where install.php remains reachable.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Sites patched for the previous Fail2Install bug (CVE-2026-132165) may still be vulnerable if the installer remained reachable.; Administrators must upgrade to Drupal 11.4.14, 11.3.23, or 10.6.23 and immediately execute update.php.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The Drupal security team says attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that lets them breach and hijack unpatched websites.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 5. Unpatched Cacti Zero-Day Enables RCE in Just Four HTTP Requests via Guest Access

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Researchers disclosed an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Cacti 1.2.31 (tracked as 4HTTP2SHELL / 4HTTP2ROOT) that enables unauthenticated remote code execution in four HTTP requests. The exploit chains a guest session parameter modification into a second-order SQL injection and popen() execution.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: A public proof-of-concept exists with no official patch or CVE assigned yet.; Administrators running Cacti must immediately disable the guest account and restrict network access to the monitoring interface.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: I found a path from a fresh, unauthenticated HTTP session to command execution as the Cacti server.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 6. Hackers Trojanize Official Q-Dir and DesktopOK Downloads to Deliver Remote Access Malware

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A software supply chain attack compromised the official SoftwareOK website, tampering with Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers to deliver remote access malware. Malicious binaries were served both via direct web downloads and through the built-in update mechanism of previously installed software.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Auto-update channels in lightweight desktop utilities remain a high-value vector for stealthy malware distribution.; Security teams should hunt for recent executions or updates of Q-Dir and DesktopOK across enterprise endpoints.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Evidence indicates that malicious files were generated not only when users downloaded the programs directly from the official download page but also during the update process.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 7. Free e-government platform that serves two billion people in ten countries has critical SQL injection bug

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Public Sector & AppSec

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: India's open-source Digital Infrastructure for Governance (DIGIT) platform contains a critical SQL injection vulnerability affecting thousands of organizations across ten countries. The modular suite handles sensitive civic functions including authentication and payment collection for up to two billion citizens.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Public sector deployments relying on DIGIT must urgently apply patches to prevent mass citizen data exposure.; Third-party modules built atop the DIGIT ecosystem should also be audited for inherited database query flaws.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: India’s free e-government platform has a critical SQL injection flaw that thousands of organizations must patch to protect up to two billion citizens.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Register

tier2.title: 8. Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Supply Chain Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Hex.pm, the package manager for the Erlang and Elixir ecosystem, patched a critical CVSS 10.0 vulnerability (CVE-2026-129514) that attackers exploited to execute commands on production web servers. While no evidence of package modification was found, database reads are unlogged, meaning user emails, password hashes, and 2FA secrets may have been exposed.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Developers using Hex.pm should rotate their credentials, API keys, and 2FA secrets immediately.; Downstream Elixir and Erlang projects should verify package integrity hashes against known good states.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A vulnerability in hex.pm allowed hackers to run commands on web servers. No evidence of data modification was found, but database reads are not logged.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SecurityWeek

tier2.title: 9. Palo Alto confirms Fragnesia exploitation against firewalls in PHP2Shell attacks

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Network & Perimeter Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Palo Alto Networks confirmed that threat actors chained the Linux kernel 'Fragnesia' flaw (CVE-2026-46300) with PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to achieve root privilege escalation on PAN-OS firewalls. The vendor shipped fixes for the underlying kernel bug six months after it was patched upstream in Linux.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Appliance vendors often lag in integrating upstream Linux kernel patches, leaving perimeter devices exposed to n-day privilege escalation.; PAN-OS administrators must apply the latest security updates and inspect devices for unauthorized root-level persistence.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that attackers exploited Fragnesia, a Linux kernel flaw, to gain root on PAN-OS firewalls through the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: CSO Online

tier2.title: 10. New GeoServer RCE exploit chain seen in the wild two days after disclosure

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Threat actors began actively probing a chain of five GeoServer vulnerabilities that enables unauthenticated remote code execution just 48 hours after public disclosure. Security firm watchTowr detected the exploitation attempts across its global honeypot network from multiple IP addresses.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Time-to-exploitation for multi-bug RCE chains continues to shrink, leaving a sub-48-hour patching window.; Organizations running internet-facing GeoServer instances must patch immediately or place instances behind strict authentication proxies.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Attackers have begun probing a chain of five GeoServer vulnerabilities that enables unauthenticated remote code execution, just two days after the open source geospatial server project disclosed the flaws.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: CSO Online

tier2.title: 11. BabidiGhost Metabase Takeovers: Inside the Actor’s Second Server

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence & AI

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Forensic analysis of a second server belonging to the threat actor BabidiGhost revealed that a single operator using a jailbroken AI agent compromised 1,093 Metabase instances over four weeks. The operation demonstrates how solo actors can achieve enterprise-scale campaign volume using autonomous AI tooling.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Jailbroken AI agents act as massive force multipliers, allowing single operators to compromise over a thousand servers in a month.; Self-hosted business intelligence tools like Metabase require strict perimeter access controls and rapid patching.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: In roughly four weeks, one French-speaking operator and a jailbroken AI agent took over 1,093 Metabase instances.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SOCRadar

tier2.title: 12. Wyoming uranium operation shuts down after cyberattack

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Critical Infrastructure & OT

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Australian producer Peninsula Energy temporarily shut down its Lance uranium project in Wyoming after a cyberattack impacted plant and wellfield control systems. The company activated incident response protocols and brought in external specialists to secure its US subsidiary, Strata Energy.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Operational technology (OT) and wellfield control systems in the energy and mining sectors remain prime targets for disruptive cyberattacks.; Industrial operators must maintain manual fallback procedures and strict air-gapping or unidirectional gateways for wellfield controls.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Peninsula Energy has temporarily shut down its Wyoming uranium operation after a 'cybersecurity incident' affected plant and wellfield control systems.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Register

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Public Sector Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The UK Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) took its online services offline as a precautionary measure following a cyber incident. Officials stated that regular pension and benefit payment disbursements have not been disrupted while investigations continue.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Government citizen-facing portals require decoupled payment processing backends to ensure continuity during front-end breaches.; Incident response plans for public utilities should prioritize transparent communication to prevent citizen panic.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The DWP said that online services had been taken offline as a precaution following a cyber-incident, regular pension and benefit payments have not been affected.

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Public Sector Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The US Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disconnected affected systems after detecting unauthorized access, marking the latest incident in a wave of breaches targeting US federal agencies. fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways

tier2.title: 15. Remus malware steals Gmail messages via fake Google Sheets extension

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Endpoint & Browser Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The Remus infostealer is exfiltrating victims' Gmail messages using a malicious Chrome extension masquerading as Google Sheets. Marketed on underground forums as a Gmail zero-day, the malware bypasses OAuth consent screens entirely by reading and exfiltrating mail directly through the browser session.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Malicious browser extensions completely bypass OAuth token controls by piggybacking on active authenticated browser sessions.; Enterprises should enforce strict Chrome extension allowlists via Group Policy or Workspace admin controls.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Operators marketed the capability as a 0-day in Google's email service; stolen mail leaves through the extension itself, no OAuth consent screen.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 16. CISA added 10 exploited flaws to KEV (Nov 25)

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA added 10 actively exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, including five flaws in Mitel MiCollab (such as CVSS 10.0 command injection CVE-2026-133323), HPE Juniper Session Smart root command injection (CVE-2026-103406), Vates Xen Orchestra auth bypass (CVE-2026-133469), and three Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller bugs.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Federal agencies face an aggressive November 28 remediation deadline for these 10 actively exploited flaws.; Enterprise teams running Mitel MiCollab, Juniper Session Smart routers, or Xen Orchestra must prioritize emergency patching.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: CISA added 10 flaws to its KEV catalog, incl. five Mitel MiCollab bugs — notably CVE-2026-133323 (CVSS 10.0), a command injection in the AWV component.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 17. ASUS Patches Critical Control Center Flaws Allowing Remote Administrative Takeover

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Enterprise Endpoint Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: ASUS patched multiple critical vulnerabilities in ASUS Control Center Express, including a CVSS 10.0 flaw caused by hard-coded cryptographic keys. The vulnerabilities allow remote unauthenticated attackers to forge authentication tokens and gain full administrative control over managed business workstations.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Hard-coded cryptographic keys in centralized IT management software create catastrophic single points of failure.; Organizations utilizing ASUS Control Center Express must apply the vendor patch immediately and restrict management console exposure.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: These vulnerabilities allow remote attackers to forge authentication tokens and gain full administrative control over managed business PCs and workstations.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: #infosec

tier2.title: 18. Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Enterprise Architecture

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Microsoft announced it will officially remove the Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) server role in Windows Server 2028, following its earlier deprecation. Meanwhile, Microsoft also pushed an emergency out-of-band hotpatch to fix Windows Server 2025 crashes caused by November's KB5131077 security update.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Enterprise IT and security teams relying on on-premises WSUS must begin planning migrations to Windows Autopatch, Intune, or third-party patch management tools.; Windows Server 2025 administrators experiencing crashes from KB5131077 should deploy the new emergency hotpatch immediately.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer
